cards.text: Jesus and His disciples are going up the road to Jerusalem, and Jesus is out front, walking ahead of all of them. The disciples are amazed, and the people following behind are afraid. Then, again, Jesus takes the Twelve aside.

cards.question: On the road to Jerusalem, Jesus pulls the Twelve aside. What does He start telling them about?

answers.text: What is going to happen to Him
Where they will stay in the city
How the temple will be rebuilt

cards.text: Jesus says it plain. They're going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man, Jesus talking about Himself, will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Twelve that the chief priests and scribes will condemn the Son of Man to death.
After condemning Him, the chief priests and scribes will hand the Son of Man over to the ___.

cards.text: Jesus doesn't soften any of it. The Gentiles will mock Him, spit on Him, flog Him and kill Him.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Twelve that after three days He will rise again.

cards.text: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come up to Jesus. They've got a request, but they don't lead with it.

cards.question: Before they say what they want, James and John tell Jesus they want Him to do for them whatever they ask.

cards.text: That's sliding a paper across your boss's desk and saying, 'Sign first. I'll tell you what it is LATER.' So Jesus asks them what they want.

cards.question: Jesus asks James and John, "What do you want Me to do for you?" What do the two of them ask for?

answers.text: Seats at His right and left

cards.text: One on His right, one on His left, in His glory. Front row, names on the chairs, NOBODY else allowed!

cards.question: Jesus tells James and John they know exactly what they're asking for.
Jesus asks James and John if they can drink the cup He will drink and be baptized with His baptism. What do the brothers answer?
Jesus tells James and John they will drink His cup and be baptized with His baptism. But what does He say about the seats at His right and left?

answers.text: They are not His to grant
They belong to Moses and Elijah
They go to the oldest disciples

cards.text: Jesus says, "These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared." Friend, I prep cookie boxes all day long, and even I don't touch the seating chart.
Then the other ten disciples hear about what James and John asked for.

cards.question: The ten find out James and John asked for the seats at Jesus' right and left. How do the ten feel about the two brothers?

cards.text: Ask the boss for the corner office, and by quitting time EVERYBODY in the building knows. So Jesus calls them all together and starts with something they already know: how the rulers of the Gentiles act.

cards.question: What does Jesus say the rulers of the Gentiles do to the people under them?
Jesus tells His disciples it should work the same way among them as it does with the rulers of the Gentiles.
Jesus says whoever wants to become great among the disciples must be their ___.
Jesus takes it even further: whoever wants to be ___ must be the ___ of all.

cards.text: Then Jesus points to the example that settles it: the Son of Man Himself.

cards.question: Jesus says even the Son of Man did not come to be served. What did He come to do?
Jesus says the Son of Man came to give His life as a ransom for many.

findings.problem: Card 8 says James and John have a request 'but they don't lead with it.' That tells the baker they open with something other than the request, so it rules out 'False' on card 9 before the baker answers. Card 9 asks whether they first ask Jesus to do whatever they ask.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Charge over the other ten' is close to the right answer, the seats at His right and left in His glory, because both are about rank above the others. The ten's indignation in 10:41 makes that reading even easier to argue. A baker could argue it is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke 'even I don't touch the seating chart' doesn't click. 'Even I' sets Papa Dorin up as someone you'd expect to have more say over the seats than Jesus, who just said they are not His to grant. 'The seating chart' also hints that the seats 'in Your glory' are seating at the Marriage Supper, a connection Mark 10:37-40 doesn't make. A reader has to stop and work out what the comparison means.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The answers don't match. 'Indignant' is the exact BSB word, so it sounds more like the Bible than 'Amused' or 'Proud of them.' 'Proud of them' is also a phrase, while the other two are single adjectives.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The wrong words 'king' and 'master' mean nearly the same as 'first' in blank 1. 'Whoever wants to be king must be the slave of all' says the same thing as the right answer, so the card tests the exact wording rather than the meaning.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
